74385-the-venetians.title: The Venetians
74385-the-venetians.creator: Unknown
74385-the-venetians.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. Little golden cloudlets, like winged living creatures, were hanging high up in the rosy glow above Santa Maria della Salute, and all along the Grand Canal the crowded gondolas were floating in a golden haze, and all the westward-facing palace windows flashed and shone with an illumination which the lamps and lanterns that were to be lighted after sundown could never equal, burnt they never so merrily.

arxiv-1809-00289.title: Opinion Conflicts: An Effective Route to Detect Incivility in Twitter Journal: PACMHCI Volume: 2 CSCW 117 1 Price: 15.00 DOI: 10.1145/3274386 Thanks: This research has been performed when SKM and AC were at IIT Kharagpur, India CCS: Human-centered computing Social media CCS: Human-centered computing
arxiv-1809-00289.creator: Suman Kalyan Maity, Aishik Chakraborty, Pawan Goyal, Animesh Mukherjee
arxiv-1809-00289.description: Abstract . In Twitter, there is a rising trend in abusive behavior which often leads to incivility 1 1 1 https://phys.org/news/2016-11-twitter-tool-curb-online-abuse.html . This trend is affecting users mentally and as a result they tend to leave Twitter and other such social networking sites thus depleting the active user base. In this paper, we study factors associated with incivility.

arxiv-1902-00140.title: Advances of Machine Learning in Molecular Modeling and Simulation
arxiv-1902-00140.creator: Mojtaba Haghighatlari, Johannes Hachmann
arxiv-1902-00140.description: Abstract In this review, we highlight recent developments in the application of machine learning for molecular modeling and simulation. After giving a brief overview of the foundations, components, and workflow of a typical supervised learning approach for chemical problems, we showcase areas and state-of-the-art examples of their deployment.

arxiv-1909-11422.title: On the Contact and Nearest-Neighbor Distance Distributions for the n n -Dimensional Matérn Cluster Process
arxiv-1909-11422.creator: Kaushlendra Pandey, Harpreet S. Dhillon, Abhishek K. Gupta
arxiv-1909-11422.description: Abstract This letter provides exact characterization of the contact and nearest-neighbor distance distributions for the n n -dimensional ( n n -D) Matérn cluster process (MCP). We also provide novel upper and lower bounds to these distributions in order to gain useful insights about their behavior.

arxiv-2104-13455.title: Testing the consistency between cosmological data: the impact of spatial curvature and the dark energy EoS
arxiv-2104-13455.creator: Javier E. Gonzalez, Micol Benetti, Rodrigo von Marttens, Jailson Alcaniz
arxiv-2104-13455.description: Abstract The results of joint analyses of available cosmological data have motivated an important debate about a possible detection of a non-zero spatial curvature. If confirmed, such a result would imply a change in our present understanding of cosmic evolution with important theoretical and observational consequences.

arxiv-2209-10993.title: Reconstruction of Point Events in Liquid-Scintillator Detectors Subjected to Total Reflection
arxiv-2209-10993.creator: Wei Dou(窦威), Benda Xu(续本达), Jianfeng Zhou(周建锋), Zhe Wang(王 吉 吉 ), Shaomin Chen(陈少敏)
arxiv-2209-10993.description: Abstract The outer water buffer is an economic option to shield the external radiative backgrounds for liquid-scintillator neutrino detectors. However, the consequential total reflection of scintillation light at the media boundary introduces extra complexity to the detector optics. This paper develops a precise detector-response model by investigating how total reflection complicates photon propagation and degrades reconstruction.

arxiv-2303-04803.title: Open-Vocabulary Panoptic Segmentation with Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
arxiv-2303-04803.creator: Jiarui Xu Sifei Liu Arash Vahdat Wonmin Byeon, Xiaolong Wang Shalini De Mello, UC San Diego
arxiv-2303-04803.description: Abstract We present ODISE: Open-vocabulary DIffusion-based panoptic SEgmentation, which unifies pre-trained text-image diffusion and discriminative models to perform open-vocabulary panoptic segmentation. Text-to-image diffusion models have the remarkable ability to generate high-quality images with diverse open-vocabulary language descriptions. This demonstrates that their internal representation space is highly correlated with open concepts in the real world.

arxiv-2406-02160.title: Word equations, constraints, and formal languages
arxiv-2406-02160.creator: Laura Ciobanu
arxiv-2406-02160.description:
A 2024 arXiv research paper by Laura Ciobanu. In this short survey we describe recent advances on word equations with non-rational constraints in groups and monoids, highlighting the important role that formal languages play in this area. 1
Introduction

The question of finding solutions to equations in algebraic structures such as semigroups, groups or rings is a fundamental topic in mathematics and theoretical computer science that finds itself at the frontier between decidability and undecidability.

arxiv-2409-17639.title: Electrification of a non-rotating black hole
arxiv-2409-17639.creator: Ken-ichi Nakao 1,2,3, Kenta Matsuo 1, Hirotaka Yoshino 1,2,3, Hideki Ishihara 2
arxiv-2409-17639.description: Abstract Zajaček et al made an interesting theoretical prediction on the electrification of a non-rotating black hole; if a non-rotating black hole is surrounded by plasma composed of protons and electrons, it will acquire electric charge due to the large difference of the inertial mass of a proton and that of an electron.

arxiv-2502-01205.title: OCR Error Post-Correction with LLMs in Historical Documents: No Free Lunches
arxiv-2502-01205.creator: Jenna Kanerva, Cassandra Ledins, Siiri Käpyaho, Filip Ginter
arxiv-2502-01205.description: Abstract Optical Character Recognition (OCR) systems often introduce errors when transcribing historical documents, leaving room for post-correction to improve text quality. This study evaluates the use of open-weight LLMs for OCR error correction in historical English and Finnish datasets. We explore various strategies, including parameter optimization, quantization, segment length effects, and text continuation methods.

arxiv-2505-03385.title: Solar Flare Forecast: A Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Algorithms for Predicting Solar Flare Classes
arxiv-2505-03385.creator: Julia Bringewald
arxiv-2505-03385.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Julia Bringewald. Solar flares are among the most powerful and dynamic events in the solar system, resulting from the sudden release of magnetic energy stored in the Sun’s atmosphere. These energetic bursts of electromagnetic radiation can release up to 10 32 10^{32} erg of energy, impacting space weather and posing risks to technological infrastructure and therefore require accurate forecasting of solar flare occurrences and intensities.

arxiv-2510-15964.title: Long Exposure : Accelerating Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for LLMs under Shadowy Sparsity
arxiv-2510-15964.creator: Tuowei Wang 1 2 3 4 , Kun Li 1 4 5 , Zixu Hao 1 2 , Donglin Bai 1 , Ju Ren 2 5 , Yaoxue Zhang 2 , Ting Cao 1 , Mao Yang 1
arxiv-2510-15964.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Tuowei Wang 1 2 3 4 , Kun Li 1 4 5 , Zixu Hao 1 2 , Donglin Bai 1 , Ju Ren 2 5 , Yaoxue Zhang 2 , Ting Cao 1 , Mao Yang 1. The adaptation of pre-trained large language models (LLMs) to diverse downstream tasks via fine-tuning is critical for numerous applications. However, the inefficiency of parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) techniques presents significant challenges in terms of time investments and operational costs.

pmc-10480450.title: Proteomic and functional characterisation of extracellular vesicles from collagen VI deficient human fibroblasts reveals a role in cell motility
pmc-10480450.creator: Carmen Badosa, Mónica Roldán, Joaquín Fernández-Irigoyen, Enrique Santamaria, Cecilia Jimenez-Mallebrera
pmc-10480450.description: Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are key mediators of cell-to-cell communication. Their content reflects the state of diseased cells representing a window into disease progression. Collagen-VI Related Muscular Dystrophy (COL6-RD) is a multi-systemic disease involving different cell types. The role of EVs in this disease has not been explored.

pmc-10524815.title: “Big Data” Analyses Underlie Clinical Discoveries at the Aortic Institute
pmc-10524815.creator: Mohammad A. Zafar, Bulat A. Ziganshin, Yupeng Li, Nicolai P. Ostberg, John A. Rizzo, Maryann Tranquilli, Sandip K. Mukherjee, John A. Elefteriades
pmc-10524815.description: This issue of the Yale Journal of Biology and Medicine (YJBM) focuses on Big Data and precision analytics in medical research. At the Aortic Institute at Yale New Haven Hospital, the vast majority of our investigations have emanated from our large, prospective clinical database of patients with thoracic aortic aneurysm (TAA), supplemented by ultra-large genetic sequencing files.

pmc-11286943.title: Accelerometer approach for anticipatory postural adjustments assessment during step initiation in patients with leprosy
pmc-11286943.creator: Yuzo Igarashi, Amelia Pasqual Marques, Karen Flaviane Assis Andrade, Aymee Lobato Brito, Marília Brasil Xavier, Givago Silva Souza, Bianca Callegari
pmc-11286943.description: Anticipatory postural adjustments (APAs) involve a complex coordination of sensorimotor information that can be impaired in diseases that affect nerve conduction. Assessing APAs typically requires costly video recording technology, posing a challenge to the study of postural changes. This hurdle is compounded in impoverished communities affected by diseases such as leprosy, which often receive limited government support.

pmc-11481467.title: Making sense together: dance improvisation as a framework for a collaborative interdisciplinary learning processes
pmc-11481467.creator: Lisa Nelson, Julien Laroche, Nara Figueiredo, João Fiadeiro, Joseph Dumit, Asaf Bachrach
pmc-11481467.description: This editorial outlines the outcome of an interdisciplinary session on collective sense-making through dance improvisation, which took place during the ‘Neural and Social Bases of Creative Movement’ workshop. We argue that joint improvisation practices place the scientist in a privileged position to reveal the nature of cognitive and creative behaviors.

pmc-11486501.title: Cardiothoracic surgery and white elephants in the room: medical neoliberalism and its consequences for patient care
pmc-11486501.creator: Hendrik Jan Ankersmit
pmc-11486501.description: se pertaining to percutaneous coronary intervention versus coronary artery bypass grafting surgery and to surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) versus transfemoral aortic valve intervention (TAVI). Prominent academic journals and academic societies take the lead in promulgating such ‘innovative therapies’ in the realm of cardiovascular therapy.

pmc-11646895.title: Right Ventricular Metastasis of Ewing Sarcoma Treated Through Surgical Resection
pmc-11646895.creator: Toshiki Yokoyama, Hiroshi Kurazumi, Ryosuke Nawata, Kazumasa Matsunaga, Ryo Suzuki, Akihito Mikamo, Kimikazu Hamano
pmc-11646895.description: A 27-year-old man diagnosed with right ventricular metastasis of Ewing sarcoma was referred to our institution. We surgically resected the metastatic tumor to prevent sudden death and reconstructed the right ventricle and tricuspid valve. He has survived for 1 year postoperatively without recurrence.

pmc-12565902.title: Effects of Biofertilizer and Green Manure on Soil Bacterial Community in Korla Fragrant Pear Orchard
pmc-12565902.creator: Jie Li, Xing Shen, Bolang Chen, Zhanyi He, Linsen Yan, Lele Yang, Bangxin Ding, Zhongping Chai, Mohamed Hijri, O Roger Anderson
pmc-12565902.description: The sustainability of Korla fragrant pear orchards has been increasingly threatened by prolonged intensive agricultural practices. In response, biofertilizers and green manures have gained attention due to their potential to enhance soil structure, activate microbial functions, and improve nutrient uptake. However, the dynamic changes in soil bacterial communities under such interventions remain inadequately understood.

pmc-13106988.title: Endoparasite Prevalence in the Mountain Bongo (Tragelaphus eurycerus spp. isaaci) at Mount Kenya Wildlife Conservancy
pmc-13106988.creator: Samuel Njuki Mahiga, Evans M. Mwangi, Robert Aruho, Joyce Omari, Paul W. Webala
pmc-13106988.description: Parasite–host interactions influence the success of wildlife reintroductions. The mountain bongo ( Tragelaphus eurycerus isaaci) is a critically endangered antelope found only in Kenya's montane forests, with fewer than 100 remaining in the wild. It is, therefore, imperative to re‐establish a viable, healthy, and self‐sustaining population in its native habitat.

pmc-13191261.title: tRNA modifications in viral replication
pmc-13191261.creator: Chathuri Pathirage, Kristin S Koutmou, Karin Musier-Forsyth
pmc-13191261.description: tRNA modifications are key players in post-transcriptional gene expression regulation under external and cellular stresses. Viral infection is a common external stress that hijacks cellular processes for replication. Host cell tRNA pools and modification profiles are often reshaped during viral infection, eliciting both pro- and anti-viral effects.

pmc-13254429.title: Clinical heterogeneity and immunotherapy outcomes in anti-GAD65 antibody-associated autoimmune encephalitis: a retrospective study
pmc-13254429.creator: Yihui Qiu, Zhiheng Huang, Tengyun Ma, Lihuan Lan, Guixian Ma, Kun Nie, Yuhu Zhang, Lijuan Wang, Jiehao Zhao
pmc-13254429.description: Anti-glutamic acid decarboxylase 65 (GAD65) antibody-associated autoimmune encephalitis (AE) is characterized by diverse neurological manifestations and systemic autoimmune comorbidities, posing diagnostic and therapeutic challenges. This study aimed to investigate the clinical heterogeneity, immunological characteristics, neuropathological features, and therapeutic outcomes in patients with anti-GAD65 AE.

pmc-13474887.title: Tubulin-tyrosine ligase-like protein 12(TTLL12): elevated expression in oral squamous cell carcinoma and its clinical prognostic implications
pmc-13474887.creator: Yu-lu Wang, Yi-run Wang, Lin-sheng Dong, Ya-dong Li
pmc-13474887.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundThe aim of the present study was to investigate the expression of tubulin-tyrosine ligase-like protein 12 (TTLL12) in oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) and to explore its potential associations with clinicopathological characteristics and patient prognosis.MethodsA total of 162 OSCC tissue samples and 30 adjacent normal tissue samples were collected from patients who underwent surgical resection at the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University between May 2014 and December 2018. Paraffin sections were prepared, and TTLL12 expression was detected via immunohistochemistry (IHC).

pmc-13615505.creator: Gema Nicolle Santander, Nicole Babbitt, Javiera Veas-Torres, Macarena Silva-Rojas, Gabriel Mingo, Andrés Valdivia, Alejandra Espinoza, Sofía Salas, Cristóbal Canales, German Cabrera, Anais Muñoz, Josefa Fuenzalida, Javiera Pradenas, Isidora Vega, Valentina George, Gabriel Maldonado, Varina Aldana, D
pmc-13615505.description: SummaryVasculogenic mimicry (VM) refers to the ability of non-endothelial cells to form fluid-conducting, vessel-like structures independently of endothelial cells. In cancer, VM is associated with tumor aggressiveness and poor prognosis, although similar structures may also be formed by non-cancerous cells.
